entities.name: Nasir Khusraw
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nasir Khusraw was a Persian Isma'ili poet, philosopher, traveler, and missionary for the Isma'ili Fatimid Caliphate, who played a crucial role in the propagation of Isma'ilism within the region from 1029 to 1088. Born in the city of Qom, Persia (modern-day Iran), Khusraw embarked on extensive travels to the Indian subcontinent, Syria, and Egypt, where he converted many locals to Isma'ilism and wrote influential works on theology and philosophy. His writings, such as the \
\nThe Book of the Balance of the Scales of Justice, had a lasting impact on Islamic thought and influenced prominent thinkers like Avicenna and Ibn Sina. Khusraw's legacy can be seen in the continued presence of Isma'ili communities in the Middle East and North Africa, as well as the enduring influence of his writings on Islamic philosophy and mysticism. Despite his significant contributions, Khusraw's life and work remained relatively unknown outside of Isma'ili circles until recent scholarly efforts to uncover his significance.
